Relief must be applied at the point of sale by the supplier; there is no post-purchase reclaim process. The app’s entire proposition, scanning receipts and generating a reclaim pack for HMRC, targets a process that doesn't exist, making the idea impossible to execute.

entries.title: SafeStep Eldercare Fall Sentry
entries.oneLiner: A solo operator performs in-home fall-risk assessments for the ageing parents of public sector workers, using a portable sensor array and a proprietary risk model, then installs low-cost monitoring sensors for ongoing remote oversight.
entries.reason: The passages show multiple existing providers already delivering in-home fall-risk/safety assessments for seniors and their families: HawkNest (PT-led assessments with a free fall-risk check), StillWell Health (nurse-led home safety reviews), and Age Safe America (an established senior-home-safety industry training advisors since 2015). The space has active incumbents serving this exact need, so it is not underserved.

entries.title: DentRefund, The Dental Bill Overcharge Challenger
entries.oneLiner: A productized dental bill audit service that benchmarks a patient's private dental charges against market rates, identifies overcharges, and sends a formal negotiation letter to recover excess fees.
entries.reason: Passage shows MyBillRX already offers the identical core value, decoding a dental bill, comparing every charge to real negotiated rates, and drafting a dispute letter, for free with no account, commoditising the analysis-plus-negotiation-letter wedge; and show the underlying rate-benchmark data is itself a sold commodity. The passages address US insurance bills rather than UK cash dentistry, so the commoditisation is shown but not proven to remove all margin in the candidate's specific market.

entries.title: SonicCrate, The Freelancer's Field Recording Library
entries.oneLiner: A subscription-based library of high-quality, location-specific ambient recordings physically captured by a solo field recordist, enriched with AI metadata for filmmakers, game designers, and podcasters who need unique, professional-tier soundscapes.
entries.reason: Quiet Planet provides pristine, field-captured nature recordings specifically for film, TV, and game producers, showing a dominant incumbent already serves this need well.

entries.title: Tenant Defend: Landlord Risk Intel
entries.oneLiner: A pay-per-report database that reveals a landlord's history of deposit disputes, repair neglect, and harassment complaints using public tribunal records and council data, giving a young renter the same vetting power landlords have always held.
entries.reason: Landlord Record aggregates UK Housing Ombudsman decisions into a searchable database, directly occupying the same niche as the proposed tenant-facing landlord intelligence product. This shows an existing service is already solving the problem, so the space is not underserved.

entries.title: The Private-Patient Price-Equivalence Index
entries.oneLiner: A hyper-local data service that maps NHS waiting times for common procedures to the nearest private hospital cash prices, delivering a weekly “Wait vs. Pay” matrix for subscribers in a region.
entries.reason: A service (TreatCompare) already offers monthly-refreshed NHS wait times by postcode mapped to private cost comparison, directly refuting the claim that this data combination is structurally unavailable or proprietary.

entries.title: LevyPass: The Apprenticeship Fund Transfer Broker
entries.oneLiner: A solo operator matches large construction firms with unspent apprenticeship levy pots to small trades businesses that want to hire apprentices but lack the levy funds, negotiating a transfer of up to 25% of the levy pot under UK rules and taking a 10% finder’s fee from the receiving employer per placed apprentice.
entries.reason: The passage indicates that the government has fundamentally overhauled the apprenticeship levy system, providing 100% funded apprenticeships for SMEs, which removes the mismatch that creates value for a levy-transfer broker.

entries.title: PlotProfit, The Public Sector Worker's Garden Income Service
entries.oneLiner: A solo operator physically harvests overlooked fruit trees and vegetable patches in public sector workers' gardens, sells the produce to local buyers, and shares the revenue with the homeowner, all powered by AI yield analytics.
entries.reason: Passage describes Hidden Harvest, an urban food harvest organization that locates and harvests existing city fruit/nuts, directly showing an incumbent already solving this need.

entries.title: PrintFit, The Gang-Run Nesting Engine for Small Print Shops
entries.oneLiner: A vertical tool that automatically nests multiple small print jobs onto press sheets to minimize paper waste and press time, turning a manual art into a one-click optimization for commercial printers.
entries.reason: The candidate's value rests on print-specific gang/true-shape nesting that allegedly 'no print MIS vendor offers,' but Griffin and Fiery Prep-it already sell print-specific true-shape nesting to cut media waste, and Pressria Bridge offers it free for gang sheets/stickers/DTF at 94.7% utilization in under a minute. The value is already commoditised, including a free option that removes the margin for a new entrant.

entries.title: PharmClaim, The Independent Pharmacy Reimbursement Arbitrage Tool
entries.oneLiner: A SaaS tool that connects to a pharmacy's management system, detects NHS prescription reimbursement underpayments, and generates a claim pack with evidence and clinical justification to recover the difference, automatically.
entries.reason: RWA Pharmacy GB already offers a Claim Pack Module that identifies underpayments and generates evidence for appeals, and its effectiveness is demonstrated in a case study showing substantial recovered revenue.

entries.title: KeyTune, The Piano Technician's Lifetime Value Maximizer
entries.oneLiner: A vertical tool that ingests a technician's client list and piano details to output personalized tuning schedules and upsell recommendations, increasing recurring revenue per client.
entries.reason: Multiple established tools (PianoPlanner, PianoCal, Gazelle) specifically serve piano technicians with scheduling, client database, and workflow features, showing the space already has dominant incumbents.

entries.title: BandUp, The NHS Pay Banding Appeal Financier
entries.oneLiner: A solo funder that spots under-banded NHS staff, bankrolls their pay appeal, and takes a cut of the backpay.
entries.reason: Passages and show unions (UNISON and others) already represent NHS staff and successfully win rebanding and backpay disputes, so an incumbent already serves the core need; Flexzo AI addresses staffing, not banding appeals.

entries.title: The Private School Fee Hardship Application Architect
entries.oneLiner: A web app that reverse-engineers a private school's internal bursary/remission criteria and builds a maximally persuasive financial picture, turning a vulnerable 'plea' into a data-backed application that matches the exact metrics the school's committee uses.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: Schools freely publish bursary policies and offer direct advice from admissions and finance staff, eliminating the need for a reverse-engineering tool. The process is confidential and rigorous; an adversarial tool that reframes finances to 'trigger discretionary funds' risks detection and disqualification. No evidence shows parents will pay, or that a solo operator can build distribution, making the tool commercially unviable.

entries.title: CareCharge Clawback, The Council Domiciliary Fee Overpayment Recovery Service
entries.oneLiner: An AI-augmented service that audits local authority care contribution demands for informal carers, identifies miscalculations under the Care Act 2014, and forces refunds on a no-win-no-fee basis.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The recovery value this service sells is already captured by a free statutory incumbent: the Local Government and Social Care Ombudsman. The passages show the LGSCO already investigates care-contribution miscalculations, UPHOLDS them, and FORCES councils to recalculate and remedy at zero cost to the carer (North Yorkshire told to recalculate ~£20k gift error; Kingston-upon-Hull found at fault on a contribution debt; charging complaints upheld). This directly refutes the candidate's commodity-premortem claim that 'free advice stops at guidance' and no body 'pursues a formal appeal with tenacity', the Ombudsman does exactly that, for free, with binding force. A 30% no-win-no-fee cut is unsellable when the same outcome is free and statutory. Second, the unit economics are inverted by the evidence the deal rests on: in the flagship overcharge case the miscalculation meant the carer should have paid MORE, not less (no clawback existed), and the affected payer had £1,000 savings against £3,000 debt and cancelled care, payer_solvency 'supported' describes broke customers and tiny recoverable periodic sums, so per-case success-fee revenue is trivial. Third, distribution scored with zero passages: there is no demonstrated low-friction channel to reach dispersed individual carers, a fatal CAC problem for a one-shot low-value transaction. Fourth, the erodible base is shrinking: councils are actively deploying standardised accuracy/AI charging tools [the passage Dorset 'Formulate', Tovie/Richmond-Wandsworth], reducing the very error stock the business mines. Free statutory value-capture + broke low-value payers + no acquisition channel collapses the business model.

entries.title: SkipMate, The Micro Waste Consolidation Broker for Trades
entries.oneLiner: A solo broker that collects small quantities of problematic construction waste (plasterboard, paint, treated wood) from multiple tradespeople on the same route, consolidates it, and delivers it to licensed facilities for a flat per‑bag fee, issuing a digital duty-of-care certificate for every load.
entries.reason: SmartClear offers fully licensed construction waste removal directly for tradespeople, serving the exact need the candidate describes, thereby showing an existing incumbent solution.

entries.title: Inheritance Tax Audit Risk Forecaster
entries.oneLiner: A personalised data report that uses FOI-extracted HMRC audit patterns to predict the likelihood of a retired person's estate being investigated for inheritance tax, enabling defensive gifting and estate structuring.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The product's core premise of using periodic FOI data to predict HMRC inheritance tax audit risk is fundamentally unviable. Sources show HMRC's enforcement infrastructure (Connect system ingesting 55 billion items from 130+ sources, a £175m Quantexa AI contract) is extraordinarily complex and opaque. External attempts to reverse-engineer triggers via FOI will produce models that are inaccurate, quickly outdated, and unable to keep pace with HMRC's evolving AI-based selection. This destroys the value proposition of a reliable risk forecast for estate planning.

entries.title: Gig Shield Medical Bill Advocate
entries.oneLiner: A service that negotiates down surprise medical bills for un- or under-insured gig workers, using AI-generated settlement letters and a proprietary database of hospital discount behavior.
entries.reason: Granted and mediloop both exist and offer medical bill reduction services identical in function to the candidate, showing that the space is not underserved.

entries.title: The Freelancer's Spotlight, Live Portfolio Audits
entries.oneLiner: A video show and subscriber newsletter where an expert host critiques real freelancer portfolios and online profiles, with full access to the critique archive and ability to submit for review behind a paywall.
entries.reason: Multiple existing video series (Will Paterson, Alexandra Fasulo) and a new curated club already provide expert portfolio critiques, so dominant incumbents exist.

entries.title: Private Parking Charge Autopsy Engine
entries.oneLiner: An app that scans a private parking ticket photo, cross-references the operator's history of losing POPLA appeals, and auto-generates a winning appeal letter that a fatigued driver simply submits.
entries.reason: Passage shows an existing AI product ('Appeal Ticket') already offers the same core value, upload a PCN photo, auto cross-reference legal checkpoints, generate an appeal, FREE and at scale (12,000+ motorists), which commoditises the £25 paid letter the candidate's value rests on. A free first-party-style AI tool performing the identical function removes the margin the durability claim depends on.

entries.title: FiberForge, The Freelance Textile Artist's On‑Demand Waste‑to‑Yarn Upcycling Service
entries.oneLiner: A solo‑operated service that receives a freelancer's fabric scraps, converts them into custom‑blend yarn or felted sheets using a proprietary mini‑mill process, and ships back a usable material ready for new creations.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The idea is dead because a near-identical service already exists: Aliona Nova offers custom hand-spun yarn from a customer's own yarn waste, directly fulfilling the same need. This indicates the market is already served, with low barriers to entry (any fiber artist can replicate the process), eroding any potential for a durable competitive wedge. All other checks returned unverifiable, providing no evidence of a sustainable advantage or unaddressed demand. Building this would offer nothing new and face immediate commoditization.

entries.title: PanePrice, The Window Cleaner's Street-View Estimator
entries.oneLiner: An app that uses Google Street View imagery to count windows and their accessibility on a property, instantly producing a binding quote based on local rate cards, saving window cleaners hours of pre-visit estimation.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The candidate's entire thesis rests on a 'technical_ip' durable wedge: a fine-tuned model to count/assess windows from Street View that 'no existing franchise has a software team to build' and that generic AI 'is not tuned' to replicate. The evidence refutes that wedge on every axis. (1) The core IP is already commodity, not proprietary: a peer-reviewed method already detects glazing/windows from Google Street View with a YOLOv9 model at 94-100% facade accuracy, and the identical 'address -> Street View -> vision model -> structured building/window attributes' pipeline is being built by solo developers and hackathon teams (Open Door LLM Tool, Revealio) and explicitly marketed as reusable across multiple verticals at trivial cost (~$125 for 150 buildings). A single developer fine-tuning YOLO/SAM is the baseline, not a moat. (2) A direct incumbent already ships the exact wedge to the exact buyer: QuoteIQ's 'Property Street View' is built into the quoting workflow for home-service businesses, surfaces access/obstacle/condition assessment for remote quoting, and is bundled at $0 extra cost, collapsing both the 'no incumbent' claim and the willingness-to-pay for a standalone tool. Google itself sells Street View Insights for at-desk infrastructure feature extraction. (3) The 'free street-view' economics that the binding-quote loop depends on are legally constrained: Google's ToS restrict bulk image downloads and the generation of street-view-image-based indices, and any commercial revenue-generating use must run on the paid Google Maps Platform, so the cost base is neither free nor unencumbered. The differentiated, defensible, free-to-run wedge does not exist; what remains is a thin feature already commoditised and already offered free inside a competing product to the same sole-trader buyer.

entries.title: CareBot Commander, The Carer's Unified Command Center
entries.oneLiner: An AI inbox scraper that reads a carer's emails, texts, and calendar to extract and centralize all care-related tasks, appointments, medications, and deadlines, then provides proactive voice-guided coordination.
entries.reason: Multiple funded AI care coordination apps (Alina, Alerivq, CareHQ) already exist and target the same fragmented communication and task management problem, showing the space is not underserved.

entries.title: CareNest, The Self‑Funder Care Home Rate Negotiator
entries.oneLiner: We negotiate non‑public discounted care home rates for self‑funding primary carers by levering a confidential database of bed desperation and competitor pricing, taking a cut of the first year’s savings.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The evidence shows that the overpayment problem is real, but freely available educational resources from RightCareHome and TreatCompare already teach self-funders how to negotiate fee discounts using public MSIF data and other legal methods. These guides directly undermine the candidate's hypothesis that primary carers 'lack the data and negotiating capital': the guides provide the data (council-considered fair rates) and negotiation strategies, enabling families to achieve savings without a broker. The candidate's differentiated database of 'stealth-gathered' discount thresholds may be unnecessary if families can simply request quotes and benchmark against MSIF, which are publicly published. Without a durable information moat and with free alternatives, a broker charging 50% of first-year savings is not worth building. Additionally, there is no evidence of a low-cost distribution channel (distribution unverifiable), making customer acquisition likely expensive. The combination of free substitutes and unproven go-to-market makes this idea dead on arrival.

entries.title: PondGuard, The Predictive Aquaculture Sentinel
entries.oneLiner: A vertical IoT+AI tool for small-scale fish and shrimp farmers that ingests low-cost sensor data, predicts lethal oxygen crashes hours in advance, and dispatches actionable alerts to prevent catastrophic stock loss.
entries.reason: AquaExchange is a funded ($8M Series B) full-stack platform combining IoT devices and AI models for shrimp farming, and eFishery deploys smart sensors at fish/shrimp ponds, showing funded rivals already serve aquaculture IoT/AI monitoring; the space is not underserved.

entries.title: PropMuse, The Solo Creator's Curated Prop Library
entries.oneLiner: A hyper-local, membership-based physical prop rental service for freelance photographers, stylists, and filmmakers, offering instant access to a rotating collection of rare, thematic props without the burden of storage or sourcing.
entries.reason: ACME Brooklyn Prop Rental (since 2010) provides prop rentals for photographers, filmmakers, and other creatives in NYC, directly refuting the claim that the space is underserved.

entries.title: The Illegal Dumper's Bounty Agent
entries.oneLiner: A solo-operated broker that helps tradespeople capture council rewards for reporting fly‑tipping, turning witness intimidation into cash by packaging evidence into payout‑ready submissions and taking a success fee.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The thesis rests on a paid, opaque, unliquidated claims process, and the evidence kills that premise three ways. (1) No grounded pain or payer: pain_reality, payer_solvency, distribution and incumbency all returned unverifiable. Source-or-die: no retrieved passage shows any witness finds claiming painful or would pay a 30% fee, so the core demand claim is unsupported and cannot PASS. (2) The 'opaque process' wedge is directly refuted by the legality source: Merton's claim path is a simple email/phone with photos, paid within 14 days, treated in confidence, there is no bureaucratic maze to package away, and 'photos or video can help' is the entire evidence bar a witness already meets. (3) The unit economics are non-viable. Rewards are tiny (£100, £200 Merton; up to £500 East Hants) and paid ONLY on successful enforcement/prosecution, a rare tail outcome against 945 incidents. A 30% contingency yields £30, £150 per success, contingent on a conviction the broker cannot influence, with councils contacting the witness directly (broker is disintermediated by design) and able to 'withdraw the scheme at any time', i.e. the supposed proprietary asset is revocable, fragmented per-council, and not durable. value_durability 'supported' only confirms a reward exists, not that a packaging service captures value. No pain, no payer, no channel, trivial revocable margin.

entries.title: The Senior Driver's Licence Retention Intelligence Pack
entries.oneLiner: A data intelligence service that uses FOI-sourced DVLA medical decision data to predict a retiree's risk of licence revocation and builds an evidence-based submission to retain driving privileges.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: No grounded evidence of a reachable, paying customer. (1) DISTRIBUTION is the decisive failure: the check returned unverifiable, not one passage shows any channel to reach the target buyer (a retiree aged 65-80 who already has a notifiable medical condition). The cited pages are the regulator's own internal staff tool, the DVLA call-for-evidence, and an insurer-database B2B contribution blog, none is a route to this senior buyer. This cohort is the hardest-to-reach, lowest-digital-adoption, shame-laden segment, and the engine found zero acquisition path. (2) PAIN_REALITY is unverifiable: passages confirm DVLA runs a casework system and publishes fitness-to-drive guidance, and that one FOI request about elderly drivers exists, but NONE shows a retiree suffering acutely or paying anyone to retain a licence. The need is asserted, never grounded. (3) PAYER_SOLVENCY is nominally 'supported' but on a single passage that proves 650,000 licences were revoked over a DECADE, a large affected population, but it shows revocation, not willingness-to-pay for a counter-evidence pack, and licence loss is typically a one-shot lifetime event (no repeat revenue). (4) VALUE_DURABILITY is unverifiable: no evidence the FOI/tribunal 'proprietary data' wedge is non-commoditised, the source material (casework system, OGL-v3-licensed guidance) is freely public, so the claimed durable moat is unproven and the data is reproducible by anyone. Net: under source-or-die and verdict-from-retrieval-only, demand, reachability, and durability are all silence-not-support. Zero distribution evidence for an unreachable, low-WTP, one-shot buyer is a kill, it cannot PASS and is not worth building.

entries.title: The Client Red Flag Radar
entries.oneLiner: A weekly scored intelligence alert for freelance creatives that cross‑references Companies House data, CCJs, winding‑up petitions, and social media payment complaints to flag high‑risk clients before a contract is signed.
entries.reason: The passage shows RecoupIQ already offers the candidate's core value, checking any UK company for risk before signing by reading 12 live UK public registers in 90 seconds with daily monitoring, and offers it for free, which undercuts a paid weekly-newsletter version of the same multi-register screening. A free real-time first-party-style aggregator doing the same job removes the margin for the proposed £15-25/month product, so the value is commoditised rather than durable.

entries.title: The Solo Tradesperson's Job Completion Bond
entries.oneLiner: A digital surety issuing micro performance bonds for residential trades jobs, guaranteeing homeowners the work will be done as agreed, priced by a proprietary risk engine that scrapes non-traditional signals like local court judgments and trade forum sentiment.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The core monetisation hypothesis, a solo tradesperson pays a premium for a performance/surety bond as a lead-converting trust signal, has zero grounded support and is actively undercut by the only on-target evidence retrieved. The single 'supported' passage (Phasely) proves the homeowner pain is real but shows it is already being solved by a live, Stripe-backed deposit-escrow substitute that has orchestrated $12.4M without issuing any bond. That substitute commoditises the proposed value AND flips the payer: escrow is funded inside the homeowner's transaction, not bought by the tradesperson, collapsing the proposed business model's revenue source. Every other gate is unverifiable on retrieval (verdict-from-retrieval-only → not 'supported'): value_durability has no passage on micro-residential bonds (only generic contractor surety underwriting); payer_solvency has no evidence a solo tradesperson will pay (the passage describes lender-held financing, again not a tradesperson-bought product); distribution has no evidence of a viable channel to fragmented solo trades; legality is unaddressed (off-target CA home-improvement code and US hurricane-repair bonds), leaving the heavily-regulated nature of issuing surety/insurance products to consumers entirely unproven. The 'proprietary data moat' (court records, forum sentiment) is asserted, never grounded. Net: pain is real but already captured by a cheaper, non-regulated escrow alternative aimed at a different payer, and no gate (durability, payer willingness, distribution, legality) clears the grounded bar. Source-or-die fails on five of six checks.

entries.title: The QuietFan Audit: Subscriber Revenue Leakage Recovery
entries.oneLiner: An AI-powered audit that scans a creator's subscriber-platform transaction logs for underpaid earnings, wrongful chargebacks and fee overcharges, filing disputes on pure contingency and compounding a dispute-intelligence moat.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: KILL on source-or-die: all six gates returned `unverifiable` with zero grounded support for the thesis, and under verdict-from-retrieval-only no PASS is possible without affirmative cited evidence. Beyond the procedural kill, the retrieved evidence actively undercuts the core moat claims. The why_now asserts 'no free platform dashboard flags these reversible deductions' and the commodity_premortem claims only 'manual review' competes, but the searches surfaced multiple shipping products already occupying the adjacent space: Payfolio auto-splits gross revenue from fees per line item and reconciles every payout against the platform's fee schedule for the same creator-platform set (OnlyFans-adjacent: Patreon, Gumroad, Twitch); Fansly AI Financial Analytics already shows 'every approval, refund, and chargeback across every creator on one screen' on live platform data; and prefilecheck confirms fee/chargeback discrepancies are framed merely as a tax-reconciliation chore, not an acute pay-to-recover pain. So the detection/visibility layer the wedge depends on is already commoditised, collapsing the 'proprietary data moat' to the only un-evidenced step, actually winning disputes, for which there is ZERO grounded proof of win-rates, creator willingness-to-pay (payer_solvency unverifiable), or a distribution route (distribution). Legality is wholly ungrounded: filing chargeback/fee disputes on a creator's behalf on a contingency fee touches platform-ToS and money-claims-handling risk that no passage clears. Pain_reality never rises above a bookkeeping/tax concern. No gate clears, the moat premise is contradicted by retrieved incumbents, and the revenue-bearing step is entirely unproven.

entries.title: The Creator's Tool Stack Report
entries.oneLiner: A quarterly, data-driven report that benchmarks creative tools through anonymized telemetry from thousands of freelance workflows, exposing which tools actually cause rework or client friction, not just features.
entries.reason: The only passage reports that freelance marketplace spend collapsed 79% since 2021, indicating the freelance economy that would fund these annual subscriptions is sharply contracting, which negates the claim that the payer segment has budget to pay.

entries.title: The Retiree Landlord Compliance Risk Monitor
entries.oneLiner: A monitoring service that scrapes 300+ local council websites for new selective licensing schemes and enforcement data, then alerts retiree landlords when their properties face imminent fines or compliance gaps.
entries.reason: The passage shows Kamma already provides exactly this service: council licensing compliance turned into 'clear actions with alerts', including 'New Licence Requirement Alerts' and '24/7 Scheme Monitoring', the same scheme-monitoring-and-alert need this candidate targets. An incumbent already owns this need.

entries.title: The Gig Worker's Medical Bill Audit & Dispute Engine
entries.oneLiner: A productized service that audits a gig worker's surprise medical bill, identifying coding errors and overcharges using a proprietary database of hospital pricing data, and delivers a ready-to-submit dispute pack to slash the bill.
entries.reason: The passage shows BillSherpa already offers the core value (line-by-line audit that finds billing errors and totals overcharge savings) completely free, instantly, with no signup, commoditising the paid audit wedge and removing the margin for a fixed-fee error-check service.

entries.title: The Solo Breeder's Litter Deposit Recovery Kit
entries.oneLiner: A pre-packaged, legally-reviewed set of contracts and deposit-collection procedures sold as a digital download to small-scale dog and cat breeders who take deposits from buyers, reducing the risk of losing money when a buyer backs out.
entries.reason: The passage shows a near-identical product already on the market, a bundle including kitten sales contracts and a deposit receipt, sold as an editable template for $9.99, indicating the value is already commoditised as cheap downloadable templates rather than durable. No passage affirms that the value is durable or defensible.

entries.title: The Bursary Blind Spot
entries.oneLiner: A subscription intelligence service that mines Charity Commission filings and school data to reveal hidden bursary opportunities, giving cash-poor professionals a strategic edge through alerts, trend analysis, and a personalized matching tool.
entries.reason: The candidate's incumbency premise (no aggregator of charity public-data intelligence exists) is contradicted by SoGood Finder AI, a funded rival that over two years assembled 'the most comprehensive database of UK charity information ever' from the same public filings, with a user-facing app, a charity-intelligence incumbent already occupies this data space, though the passage does not confirm it specifically targets bursary matching.

entries.title: BakeCost Live, The Bakery Margin Autopilot
entries.oneLiner: A tool that syncs with real-time supplier price feeds and commodity futures to update recipe costs continuously, alerting the bakery owner when margins breach thresholds and suggesting price adjustments.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The candidate's entire thesis rests on a falsifiable wedge claim: that this is the 'first vertical cost-to-menu automation' and that incumbents 'focus on order management, not continuous supply-chain cost automation.' The gathered passages refute that directly. PurchasePlus already sells the exact mechanism: it 'links each recipe directly to live supplier pricing' so 'every affected dish recalculates automatically' and exposes GP% by dish/menu/outlet, explicitly framed against 'stale cost data' and 'recipe spreadsheet hasn't been updated.' INAYA Product Composer goes further into the candidate's own differentiator, binding each BOM line to 'a live index, a contract or a supplier quote,' rebuilding unit cost on every new quote, and projecting per-SKU cost against bull/base/bear price paths, i.e. the commodity-futures curve feature pitched as novel here. Expana IQ provides live AI cost-model building and finished-goods cost approximations for the same procurement/pricing job. So the only grounded verdict in the whole set, pain_reality=supported, is supported precisely BY a commercial incumbent already solving it. The 'continuous feed vs periodic spreadsheet' insight is real but already productized by at least three live vendors, and the claimed moat (a defensible proprietary baking-ingredient price dataset / switching cost) has zero grounding. value_durability, incumbency, payer_solvency, and distribution all came back unverifiable, meaning no passage shows a single-site or 1-5-location bakery owner has the budget, motive, or a reachable channel to buy a thin bakery-skinned wrapper over capabilities already sold horizontally. The residual differentiation is a vertical UI skin, not a durable wedge.

entries.title: The Council Tax Band Challenge Intel Pack
entries.oneLiner: An online intel tool for asset-rich, cash-poor retirees that predicts their UK council tax band reduction success probability and auto-generates an FOI-backed, tribunal-ready challenge argument, as VOA digitisation opens a data battlefield.
entries.reason: The passage is itself published by 'BandCheck', a service that compiles council tax challenge success rates from official sources and analyses 'where appeals work best', the same predictive-intelligence value the candidate proposes, showing a rival already operates in this exact niche. This negates the claim that the space is open/underserved.

entries.title: The HMRC Valuation Heat Map
entries.oneLiner: A proprietary database and report revealing trends in HMRC probate valuation challenges, helping retirees pre‑empt family inheritance disputes.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The candidate's entire wedge is a single falsifiable claim in its own commodity_premortem: 'No single law firm collects cross-case FOI data to build a predictive heat map.' The evidence refutes this directly. The source (Irwin Mitchell IHT Report) states they 'submitted Freedom of Information (FoI) requests to HMRC' and the report 'analyses seven years of data across the UK's 121 postcode areas, highlighting emerging trends', i.e. a law firm has already built and published the exact FOI-sourced, postcode-granular IHT heat map proposed here, and gives it away free as private-client lead-gen. The proposed moat ('proprietary_data', 'intelligence HMRC cannot itself publish') is therefore neither proprietary nor scarce: it is a free marketing asset for firms whose economics reward giving it away to win advisory clients. The source (Swift Values) shows the same pattern, a valuation firm publishing free national probate-valuation survey data as a funnel. A £30-£49 one-off report cannot out-resource a national law firm's free FOI report, and a retiree facing a real five/six-figure valuation dispute will buy a £300-£700 RICS surveyor report or solicitor, not a static trend PDF that does not value their specific estate. So while pain_reality (0.73) and value_durability-phenomenon (0.487) confirm the IHT problem is real and growing, the product's differentiation is dead on arrival: the durable-data wedge already exists for free from better-resourced incumbents, and the three commercial gates (incumbency, payer_solvency at 0.0, distribution at 0.0) returned no passage affirming an open space, a willing payer, or any channel to the retiree cohort. Real problem, but this packaging captures none of the value.

entries.title: CropSync, The Microgreens Harvest Scheduler
entries.oneLiner: A planting schedule optimiser that tells microgreens growers exactly what to plant and when, based on their restaurant clients’ demand forecasts and grow‑system parameters, to eliminate waste and guarantee reliable weekly harvests.
entries.reason: The passages show multiple purpose-built microgreens crop-planning tools already serving this exact niche, SeedLeaf ('THE PROFESSIONAL CHOICE FOR MICROGREENS CROP PLANNING AND ORDER MANAGEMENT', weekly crop production planning) and Grown Like A Pro (460+ features, AI-powered scheduling, free to start), negating the candidate's positive claim that no existing tool solves microgreens scheduling and that the value is a durable, uncommoditised wedge.

entries.title: The Probate Inventory & Valuation Toolkit
entries.oneLiner: A mobile app for probate clearance professionals that uses camera and AI to automatically catalogue household contents, assign defensible resale or charity‑donation values, and generate a formal inventory report ready for executors.
entries.reason: At least three rivals already solve AI-powered estate/probate inventory: ClearHeir offers AI-assisted cataloging and 'defensible estate inventories' for probate court filing, EstateGenie extracts items from a walkthrough video and delivers valuations, and SnapFind catalogs estate belongings. The space is occupied, not underserved.

entries.title: ShelfPrice, The Indie Bookshop Scanner
entries.oneLiner: A mobile app that lets independent bookshop owners instantly price used books by scanning barcodes, auto-grading condition via AI, and suggesting a competitive local retail price based on a cooperative data pool of anonymised sales from participating shops.
entries.reason: The passage shows Upright Books (Upright Lister), an existing AWS-powered platform built for booksellers that lets them scan, list, price, and manage inventory, which directly occupies the scan-and-price-for-booksellers space ShelfPrice targets. This negates the claim that the space is underserved.

entries.title: RainDay Cover, Parametric Weather-Action Guarantee for Outdoor Tradespeople
entries.oneLiner: A solo-operated daily weather guarantee that pays a cash benefit automatically when a pre‑specified rainfall threshold is met at the job site, no claims forms, no adjusters, just a weather API trigger.
entries.reason: The passages name at least two operating rivals, WeatherIt Rain Insurance and Sensible Weather, already delivering the exact parametric mechanism (automatic fixed cash payout when rainfall hits a trigger, no claims/adjusters), so the parametric-weather-payout space is already served by funded incumbents rather than underserved.

entries.title: The Hospital Charity Care Application Advocate
entries.oneLiner: A done-for-you service that applies for hospital charity care, using a proprietary database of each hospital’s income thresholds, documentation tricks, and appeal processes, and takes a contingency fee only on debt avoided.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The candidate's entire thesis rests on a 'proprietary_data' wedge (hospital-by-hospital income thresholds, documentation tricks, appeal paths) monetised via contingency fee. The gathered evidence refutes that wedge on both halves. (1) The free alternative the candidate names as weakest is actually its grave: Dollar For is a free nonprofit that already does the full done-for-you navigation and application of hospital financial assistance at scale, 36,000+ patients helped and over $120M in medical debt crushed, with a public goal of eliminating $1B by 2028. That is precisely the 'transplant grant-writing into healthcare' service proposed, already operating for free with a compounding national caseload no solo advocate can outpace. (2) The supposedly-proprietary database is already published for free: BillKarma gives state-by-state income limits, the documents to bring, and 'exactly what to say' to trigger the hospital's legal obligation, collapsing the information-asymmetry the service claims to own. With the durable wedge commoditised by free, well-funded incumbents, the contingency-fee model is squeezed from both sides: the payers are by definition low-income (below 200-400% FPL, ~$37k, 75k) uninsured workers, and payer_solvency, pain_reality, distribution, and incumbency all came back unverifiable, no grounded evidence that this buyer will pay a fee for what Dollar For and BillKarma already provide free. value_durability's 'supported' verdict is built on the very passage (Dollar For) that destroys the moat.

entries.title: VetScript, The Solo Vet's Controlled Drug Register Autopilot
entries.oneLiner: A plug-in that auto-populates the controlled drug log from practice management software, flags discrepancies, and pre-fills regulatory inspection reports, built for independent vet practices.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The entire thesis rests on a false premise: that PMS vendors ignore this niche and a 'solo vertical tool' can be first to build automated, PIMS-integrated controlled-drug logging with discrepancy flags and inspection-ready reports. The evidence shows that exact product already exists commercially and in near-clone form. VetSnap is a live commercial veterinary controlled-drug log that 'automates time-consuming logging and reconciliation,' 'seamlessly integrates with industry-leading PIMS,' and 'automatically flags potential log errors', feature-for-feature the candidate's pitch, already shipping with named DVM testimonials. VetRxVault is closer still: per-dose logging with practitioner sign-off, a discrepancy engine across 47 reconciliation checkpoints, auto-generated DEA 222 forms and biennial inventory reports, native PMS sync via a VetBridge connector, and a sub-90-second unannounced-inspection package, i.e., the candidate's 'switching-cost moat' built and described as 'the software that should have existed a decade ago.' Adjacent incumbents reinforce a crowded, commoditising space: PreferredMD for medical facilities and Optum's eCDR that 'automatically populates controlled drug information in real-time, further reducing discrepancies'. The pain is real and the value durable, but that cuts against the candidate: the demand is already proven AND already served by veterinary-specific incumbents, so the differentiating wedge (deep PMS integration + auto inspection reports as a novel moat) does not exist. Meanwhile payer_solvency (no passage on vet-practice budgets) and distribution (no route-to-practice shown) are both unverifiable, there is zero grounded evidence the solo vet will pay or can be reached, while there is direct evidence the moat is already occupied. A me-too vertical entering behind VetSnap and VetRxVault with no demonstrated distribution edge or willingness-to-pay is not worth building.

entries.title: The Home Extension Planning Advantage Engine
entries.oneLiner: A self-serve web app that generates objection-resistant planning applications for UK loft conversions and side extensions, powered by a predictive model trained on thousands of local refusal patterns and appeal outcomes scraped from council portals.
entries.reason: The passage shows a free-to-start tool already delivering the candidate's core 'proprietary' value for London, official planning data, local precedent, build potential, and a likelihood read ('Rear extension likely to be a workable route', a 78 planning score) before spending on consultants. This indicates the intelligence layer is being commoditised, though the tool is London-only and freemium rather than a total free substitute removing all margin for an England-wide £249 submission pack.

entries.title: The Carer's Clawback Defender
entries.oneLiner: A solo-operated service that acts as an adversarial negotiator for primary carers facing welfare benefit overpayment demands, leveraging proprietary strategies to reduce or eliminate clawbacks for a success-based fee.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The payer is structurally insolvent and the wedge is being legislated away. The buyer is, by the candidate's own framing, a primary carer under 'immense financial and emotional strain'; the only carer in evidence faces a ~£16,000 clawback he 'doesn't know how to settle', i.e. the target customer cannot fund a success-fee, and a success fee only pays if savings materialise, which is uncertain against DWP. payer_solvency is unverifiable: there is zero evidence carers have budget or willingness to pay an adversarial negotiator, and strong reason (precarity) to believe they cannot. Distribution (0.43) and legality (0.0) are also unverifiable, no route to reach isolated carers and no confirmation a success-fee adversarial service against a state benefits agency is even lawful or licensable. Meanwhile value_durability is only weakly supported (0.4) and actively decaying: the Nov 2025 Independent Review and Government response 'secured significant change that we hope will reduce the likelihood of overpayments in future', so the state is remediating the exact discrepancy this business arbitrages, shrinking the future deal flow. Incumbency: free Citizens Advice / welfare-rights advisers already navigate this complexity for carers, and there is no evidence a paid solo operator beats them. Net: a real pain (supported 0.46) attached to a broke, hard-to-reach payer, an unproven legal margin, and a wedge the government is closing. The economics do not exist.

entries.title: FreshPlot, The Nurse's Suburban Micro-Farm
entries.oneLiner: A solo operator converts an NHS worker's backyard into a hands-free, AI-optimised kitchen garden that delivers a weekly harvest box, all for a flat monthly subscription, starting with a tight 20-home cluster in a single city.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The idea cannot clear the filter and is dead on a publication decision (source-or-die). The thesis is entirely load-bearing on two claims, that NHS nurses feel acute pain from being unable to maintain a garden, and that they will pay £80-120/month for a harvest-box subscription, and BOTH returned `unverifiable` with zero supporting passages. Verdict-from-retrieval-only means no grounded demand exists: pain_reality's only hit (Li Xia's hydroponic story) and payer_solvency's only hit (Home Harvest) say nothing about UK nurses' budget, willingness, or motive to pay. With no evidence the payer exists or will pay, the economics (single operator, 20-30 homes, £80-120/mo each) are unfounded. Worse, the one commodity passage actively undercuts the model: Home Harvest is a funded tech company selling a self-contained automated home-growing unit for a one-off ~£339 plus seed mats, a cheaper, scalable, no-labour substitute for a £960-1,440/year hands-on subscription. The proprietary-microclimate-data 'switching-cost moat' is asserted but unverifiable (shows AI gardening knowledge is already free/open-), and gardening AI is broadly commoditised. The only `supported` verdict is legality, i.e. it's merely legal to run, which is not a reason to build. No gate clears affirmatively except legality; the demand foundation is ungrounded and the value is exposed to a cheaper commodity device.

entries.title: The Overage Clause Detector for Conveyancers
entries.oneLiner: A vertical tool that ingests scanned historical title deeds (even handwritten) and automatically flags dormant overage or development clawback clauses, producing a plain-English risk report that alerts conveyancing solicitors to future liabilities their standard Land Registry search would miss.
entries.reason: Multiple funded rivals already apply AI/OCR to scanned deeds and title records: V7 Go's AI Deed Analysis Agent explicitly extracts encumbrances from scanned historical deeds, while Enverus and TitleFocus offer AI title-record analysis at scale, so the AI-deed-parsing space is not open. None target the exact UK overage/clawback niche, but funded incumbents already occupy the underlying capability.

entries.title: The Property Tax Appeal Evidence Builder
entries.oneLiner: A web tool that equips US homeowners to fight assessment increases by generating a county-compliant comparable-sales evidence packet and appeal letter, using proprietary local market data and argument templates.
entries.reason: The exact value proposed for a flat fee, generating a comparable-sales/comp evidence packet and appeal kit, is already given away free by direct substitutes: one explicitly a 'free alternative to paid comp-report services' and another 'Free. All features included. No subscription, no in-app purchases', with a third instantly generating a county-specific challenge kit. Free tools doing the identical job remove the margin for a paid entry.

entries.title: Call‑Back Shield, The Tradesperson’s Workmanship Guarantee
entries.oneLiner: A solo‑operated risk‑financing service that lets a high‑quality UK tradesperson offer a six‑month defect‑free guarantee to every client, while the solo assumes the cost of any remedial call‑back using a proprietary tradesperson‑quality dataset and a curated fixer network.
entries.reason: The passage shows Magnifi Vault already offers a 'Risk Architecture' for home service contractors that structures customer callbacks and minor property damage claims, i.e. a rival already serving the exact callback-risk-financing need, so the space is not unoccupied.

entries.title: Chargeback Autopsy & Defense Engine
entries.oneLiner: A vertical AI tool that helps small e-commerce sellers build compelling chargeback rebuttal packs with data-driven argument templates, increasing win rates and reducing revenue loss.
entries.reason: Passage shows RapidResolve, a direct rival offering the same value prop, AI-built, card-network-tailored chargeback evidence packets for SMB merchants, so the space already has an active competitor and is not unserved. Confidence is tempered because RapidResolve is pre-launch ('Join the Waitlist', 'be among the first'), so no incumbent yet demonstrably owns or solves the need.

entries.title: The Creative IP Watchdog
entries.oneLiner: A paid weekly intelligence briefing for commercial illustrators and stock photographers that tracks copyright lawsuits, DMCA takedowns, and licensing shifts, translated into actionable per-use fee benchmarks and contract clauses.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: A live, FREE incumbent already occupies this exact niche, gutting the core defensibility thesis. airightsbrief.com delivers plain-English AI-image-rights briefings PLUS a practical toolkit (contract language, forms, records, client-communication templates) to the identical buyer set the candidate names: photographers, illustrators, designers, stock contributors. It even runs a free daily digest tracking litigation and licensing stories for these creators. This directly refutes the commodity_premortem's central claim that 'no one aggregates... for indie creators' and that a generalist 'cannot replicate' the wedge. The free layer commoditizes the briefing-plus-contract-clause bulk of the product, leaving only the unproven 'per-use fee benchmark / anonymized survey' data as differentiation. Against that, value_durability is unverifiable (0.44) precisely because a free first-party rival to the same audience exists; payer_solvency is unverifiable (0.40) with zero evidence any creator pays above free; and pain_reality, while supported (0.46), is satisfied for FREE by the incumbent, eliminating willingness-to-pay. A solo paid weekly newsletter charging for what a funded free competitor gives away to the same niche faces a fatal CAC and pricing-power problem.

entries.title: The Divorce Financial Forensics Engine
entries.oneLiner: A web app that flags hidden assets and drafting errors in Form E financial disclosures by cross-referencing the user's submission against a proprietary database of judicial findings from published divorce cases.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The product's entire reason to exist is the demand-side bet, that fearful squeezed-middle self-reppers will pay for hidden-asset red flags on Form E, and every demand-side check came back with ZERO grounding: pain_reality (unverifiable), payer_solvency (unverifiable), distribution (unverifiable), and legality of mining/cross-referencing UK Form E against published judgments (unverifiable). Under source-or-die and verdict-from-retrieval-only, no fetched passage shows this buyer exists, pays, can be reached, or that the data play is lawful, so the idea cannot clear the PASS bar, a KILL on the cheapest decisive gates. Worse, the ONLY grounded value point actively undercuts the consumer wedge: the passages that supported value_durability are existing commercial AI disclosure-analysis tools, firmadapt's automated family-law disclosure analysis and Disclosure Assistant's systematic cash-withdrawal/anomaly detection, but both target ATTORNEYS and LAW FIRMS, not the self-representing squeezed-middle individual this product names as its payer. So the real, grounded value is already being captured by lawyer-facing incumbents, while the free consumer-grade tooling that actually reaches individuals is a blank form generator with no anomaly detection. The 'proprietary judicial-findings database' moat is asserted, never evidenced: no passage shows such a corpus is extractable, accurate, or that consumers (not their solicitors) would act on its 'red flags.' Net: the supply side is commoditised toward lawyers, the consumer demand/pay/reach/legality side is wholly unproven, and the differentiating data moat is unverifiable. Nothing here can publish.

entries.title: The Upholsterer's Yardage & Quote Engine
entries.oneLiner: A tool that converts photos and measurements of a furniture piece into a cutting-optimised fabric yardage requirement, work order, and client quote for independent upholsterers.
entries.reason: The core value (pattern-repeat yardage calculation and cutting/nesting optimisation for furniture makers) already exists as free or commodity tools: is a free upholstery yardage calculator with pattern-repeat allowance on 54-inch goods, is a free yardage tool handling pattern repeats and cutting layouts across widths, and (CutWize) does roll-nesting optimisation and offcut tracking specifically for furniture makers, contradicting the premortem's claim that no incumbent handles geometry or pattern matching.

entries.title: The Noise Nuisance Evidence Pack Agent
entries.oneLiner: A solo operator deploys calibrated sound-level loggers in complainants' homes, retrieves them after a monitoring period, and produces a structured evidence pack for submission to the local council under statutory nuisance legislation.
entries.reason: The passages show multiple existing providers already deliver calibrated, court/legal-grade noise-nuisance evidence systems for complaints, NNR's Class 1 'legal-grade compliance' monitoring, Campbell Associates' 'robust evidence' resident-deployable systems, and Acoustilog's calibrated long-term recordings 'proven as powerful evidence in court'. Incumbents already serve the evidence-pack need, so the space is not open.

entries.title: The Radon Risk Certifier, Mobile Home Sampling
entries.oneLiner: A solo operator physically places and retrieves alpha‑track radon detectors in homes during property purchases, ensuring strict tamper‑proof chain of custody and delivering a risk‑assessed report with mitigation recommendations.
entries.reason: Passage shows 'Professional Home Testers' already perform alpha-track radon testing for real estate transactions (results used to release escrow funds), and confirms licensed radon measurement professionals perform tests including for property contexts, so professional, real-estate-facing radon testers already serve this need.

entries.title: The Home Care No-Show Claim Agent
entries.oneLiner: A contingency-fee service that extracts cash compensation from care agencies when a commissioned carer visit is missed, using a legally robust claim model built on contract law and a growing private database of successful settlements.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: Every one of the six gates returns unverifiable with zero supporting passages for the core thesis, that primary carers suffer acute, compensable financial injury from missed visits and that care agencies pay cash settlements to them. Under source-or-die / verdict-from-retrieval-only, that absence alone blocks PASS. Worse, the retrieved evidence actively cuts against the premise on three pillars. PAYER/MONEY-FLOW: the only real claim-recovery case in care contracts runs the OPPOSITE direction, a law firm recovering £45k of fees owed TO a provider from a commissioner, with no instance of agencies paying carers for no-shows; the Ombudsman, the one body actually adjudicating these disputes, issues apologies and systemic remedies, not individual cash redress. PAIN: the one substantive missed-visit source frames it as a revenue leak for the AGENCY, not an injury to the primary carer who would supposedly pay; the carer-side cases are about overcharging and unclear logs, not missed-visit compensation. DISTRIBUTION: the only acquisition evidence is agencies buying care clients via Google Ads at $800-2,000/client, no channel to reach the primary carer as buyer, and that CPC is brutal. LEGALITY and VALUE_DURABILITY have no grounding at all. The 'proprietary database of settlements' moat is unfalsified and unevidenced; nothing shows agencies settle pre-ombudsman, which is the load-bearing assumption of why_now. With no grounded pain, no demonstrated payer, an inverted money flow, no buyer channel, and an unverified legal model, the idea cannot clear the filter.

entries.title: The Funeral Price Decryptor
entries.oneLiner: A solo‑produced, hyper‑local price intelligence service that continuously tracks and decodes hidden funeral home costs through mystery shopping and web scraping, providing pre‑need planners with a personalised negotiation blueprint and savings estimate.
entries.reason: Passage shows an existing service already aggregates and publishes real funeral-home prices across 1,000 homes in 45 states, and notes the FTC Funeral Rule already mandates itemized price disclosure on request, so the core 'decode hidden funeral prices' value is already being commoditised by a broad, non-proprietary substitute rather than being a defensible unique dataset.

entries.title: The Freelance Confidence Barometer
entries.oneLiner: A monthly sentiment index and data report derived from a proprietary panel of 2,000+ creative freelancers, sold to gig platforms, policymakers, and freelancers as the definitive early‑signal of rate trends and demand shifts.
entries.reason: Passage shows Human Cloud already runs a continuous 'Freelance Market Pulse,' polling 200+ companies and freelancers across 50 countries to benchmark the freelance industry's sentiment and conditions, which is the same cross-market freelance index the candidate proposes. An incumbent is already serving this need.

entries.title: The Pop-Up Permit Packager
entries.oneLiner: A web-based vertical tool that instantly assembles a complete temporary event notice (TEN) application for alcohol-selling market stalls and pop-ups, auto-populating site plans, customizing event management plans, and selecting the local council’s exact phrasing to drastically reduce rejection rates.
entries.reason: The passages show Barnab, a platform that automates government bureaucracy and already offers a dedicated TEN product covering exactly this need (selling alcohol at pop-up bars/events), directly competing with the candidate. The space is therefore not underserved; an incumbent already addresses TEN applications for alcohol-selling pop-ups.

entries.title: The Sublease Fine Negotiator
entries.oneLiner: A done-for-you service that negotiates down or eliminates fines imposed by landlords for unauthorized subletting, using tenancy law leverage and pre-built settlement templates.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The product is premised on an instrument the evidence does not show exists. Its wedge is negotiating down or eliminating 'fines' a landlord imposes for unauthorized subletting, borrowing the parking-ticket model. But every grounded passage on the landlord's actual remedy describes EVICTION, not a negotiable fine: California treats unauthorized subletting as the most common lease violation whose 'legal remedy is an eviction' via a three-day notice to perform covenants or quit and unlawful detainer; a tenant-only firm confirms landlords serve a '3-Day Notice to Perform Covenant or Quit, then file unlawful detainer'; the landlord guide frames enforcement as detection plus the eviction process, with no fine schedule to bargain over. There is no monetary penalty to discount, so 'negotiate the fine down' has nothing to act on. The real, grounded pain is loss of possession, i.e. eviction defense, which is adversarial licensed legal practice, not a 'pre-built settlement template' + non-lawyer negotiation play (unauthorized-practice and quality risk); the cited tenant-side help is a law firm offering case-specific defense, not a templatized service. Supporting weaknesses: payer_solvency is unverifiable with zero on-point evidence that a cost-of-living-stressed Gen Z renter has budget or willingness to pay; incumbency is unverifiable because no passage shows the tenant-side fine-defense space is open OR served, so the 'free helplines can't capture this' moat claim is unproven; and the one 'supported' distribution signal (0.51) is built entirely from LANDLORD-targeting intake channels, not the buyer this product names. Net: the headline mechanism is contradicted by the law it relies on, the genuine adjacent need is licensed eviction defense outside this format, and payer willingness is unproven.

entries.title: The Travel Insurance Claim Denial Predictor
entries.oneLiner: A data intelligence tool that predicts the likelihood of a travel insurance claim being denied for a retiree’s pre-existing condition, by cross-referencing policy wordings with a proprietary database of past Financial Ombudsman Service decisions.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: Zero of six checks cleared: every gate returned 'unverifiable' (pain_reality, payer_solvency, value_durability, distribution, incumbency, legality). Under source-or-die and verdict-from-retrieval-only, silence is not support, an idea with no grounded affirmation of pain, payer, or durability cannot pass. The substance compounds the absence: (1) PAYER, the only payer-side evidence (Verisk/Ipsos) measures INSURER demand for inclusive underwriting and retiree willingness to switch POLICIES, never retiree willingness to pay a third party for a denial-prediction score; the stated buyer (anxious retiree pre-purchase or post-rejection) is entirely unproven. (2) INCUMBENCY, Verisk already operationalises pre-existing-condition risk intelligence at the point of sale (Travel Risk Rating Tool, ICD-coded condition→claim matching via API); a well-funded data incumbent owns the underwriting side and could face-flip a consumer view far faster than a solo can build a FOS scrape moat. (3) DISTRIBUTION, no low-friction channel to reach retirees is evidenced; the cohort is reached today through insurers and brokers, the very parties the product is adversarial to. (4) PAIN, no passage shows consumers acutely pay to predict denial; the only condition-specific signal is insurer-framed (existing conditions as 'the barrier in the road' to capturing the 55+ market). (5) MOAT/DURABILITY, value_durability is unverifiable; the 'proprietary FOS dataset' thesis has zero grounding that the moat resists commoditisation, and FOS decisions are public, so any competitor can scrape the same corpus. The candidate fails the publication bar on absence of grounding alone, and the available passages point insurer-side, not consumer-payer-side, on every dimension that matters.

entries.title: Gigflow City Arbitrage Index
entries.oneLiner: A solo-operated data service that ranks UK cities by net take-home for gig delivery riders after platform fees and living costs, giving Gen‑Z a personalised relocation map to maximise earnings.
entries.reason: The passage shows an existing 2026 'Net Pay Calculator Ranking' that already ranks cities by gig (DoorDash) net pay after expenses, which is the same need this candidate proposes to serve, so an incumbent already occupies the space. The candidate is UK-specific while the cited incumbent is US-based, but it is the same product category already being solved.

entries.title: SolarSurety, Micro Output Guarantee for Residential PV Installers
entries.oneLiner: A solo risk‑financing firm that guarantees the first‑year kWh output for a solar installer, using a parametric index and weather adjustment, paying out automatically if generation falls short, turning a installers’ sales risk into a fixed‑fee service.
entries.reason: The space is not open: passage names kWh Analytics as the 'market leader in Climate Insurance' with a Solar Revenue Put guaranteeing solar output, and documents an established Parametric Solar Irradiance Insurance Market with a Residential application segment and online/broker distribution. Funded incumbents already solve parametric solar-output guarantees, including the residential tier the candidate targets.

entries.title: The Concrete Colour-Match Service
entries.oneLiner: A solo operator with a spectrophotometer and a mobile mixing rig provides on-site colour-matched concrete patching for paving contractors, charging a premium per patch to eliminate the 'ugly grey scar' that costs them rework or lost client referrals.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: Every one of the six gates returned `unverifiable` with zero grounded support, which under source-or-die and verdict-from-retrieval-only is itself the kill: nothing about this idea could be confirmed from any fetched passage. Worse, the retrieved evidence actively undercuts the thesis. pain_reality: the only on-point source (HunterLab) frames concrete colour variance as a QA problem for cement manufacturers measuring batches, not paving contractors paying to erase patch 'scars', the supposed sufferer/payer never appears. incumbency + payer_solvency: the single passage describes colour-mismatch pain in field-trial batching but names no contractor willing to pay a premium and confirms no open service lane, it is vendor content selling spectrophotometers, evidence of an instrument market, not a service market. distribution: the closest source is generic 'start a concrete business' marketing with no low-friction route to paving contractors. value_durability and legality grounded on nothing relevant (a Chinese spectrophotometer spec sheet and an Iowa DOT mixer-calibration memo). The 'data moat' from a local colour database is an unsupported assertion in the hypothesis, not evidence. With no grounded payer, no demonstrated acute pain in the target segment, no distribution mechanism, and no confirmed open lane, the idea cannot clear a single hard gate. Publish-on-PASS is impossible; this is a KILL.

entries.title: The Funeral Plan Redress Enforcer
entries.oneLiner: A solo operator audits legacy pre-paid funeral plans for mis-selling or overcharging, pursues the provider for a refund on a contingent fee, and arms the carer-executor with a proprietary dossier of regulatory enforcement precedents.
entries.reason: The fee is 25% of the recovered refund, but the only grounded payment-capacity evidence shows a £2,500 plan yielded a refund of under £100 after the provider collapsed, so in the candidate's core 'provider flight / sink plan' scenario the recovery pool the fee draws from is gutted to near-zero. Strong motive is shown (anger, 'fighting'), but the payer's budget for a contingent fee is structurally absent where money has already been dissipated.

entries.title: The Freelancer's Rate Radar
entries.oneLiner: A daily intelligence brief that scrapes, normalizes, and forecasts creative freelance rates across 12 disciplines, giving independent solos the same pricing power as agencies.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The candidate's entire thesis rests on one claim: that a proprietary, cross-platform freelance rate index is a defensible data moat because incumbent platforms 'cannot follow without cannibalizing their fee structures.' The gathered evidence directly refutes that premise. YunoJuno, a funded market-leading freelancer platform (named 'highest designated Leader in Everest Group's FEMS PEAK Matrix 2026'), already publishes a free, comprehensive cross-discipline rate benchmark drawing on 182,000+ contractor/booking/skills data points across UK day rates and US hourly rates, segmented by discipline, experience and region. That free report is already being syndicated and editorialized by third parties like Freelance Informer, meaning the exact 'rate intelligence across disciplines' value proposition is in-market, free, larger-scale, and platform-published. The data moat is not durable and the 'incumbents cannot capture this' wedge is false on its face. Compounding this, the payer-solvency evidence cuts against the $19/mo subscription: more than half of creative freelancers report rising stress as budgets tighten and unpaid work grows, so the target segment is contracting discretionary spend, not adding paid intelligence subscriptions. A $19/mo premium tier of templated charts/scripts sits as a thin, scrapeable wrapper above a free incumbent benchmark sold to a financially squeezed audience. No passage establishes durable value, acute willingness-to-pay, or a defensible position; the on-point evidence that does exist points the other way.

entries.title: The Subbie's Adjudication Stake
entries.oneLiner: A solo operator provides no-win-no-fee funding for UK construction subcontractors to pursue unpaid invoices through statutory adjudication, using AI to assess claim merits and automate filings, in return for a percentage of recovered amounts.
entries.reason: The passage shows MPG already offers no-win-no-fee construction adjudication with a success-fee model (12%+VAT on ≤£200k recovered), i.e. a direct rival is already serving the unpaid-invoice adjudication need rather than the space being open.

entries.title: The Care Home Notice-Period Escape Broker
entries.oneLiner: A solo broker who matches families stuck in a care home notice period with families on the waiting list, facilitating an early contract transfer and capturing a fee from the saved rent.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The idea fails source-or-die at its two cheapest, most decisive gates. PAIN_REALITY is wholly ungrounded (verdict unverifiable): across targeted retrieval, not one passage shows any family suffering from, or paying to solve, the specific 'notice-period escape' problem (paying 4-8 weeks rent in lieu after a resident dies/leaves). Every fetched source is about the ENTRY side of care (finding/comparing/placing into a home: Erika Crossley, Appa Care, RightCareHome), never the exit-side sunk-cost the whole thesis rests on. Per Prospector's verdict-from-retrieval-only rule, silence on the pain = unverifiable, and an unverifiable core pain cannot PASS. LEGALITY is likewise 0.0/unverifiable, and the only on-topic passages actively undercut the 'tradable asset' premise: the care contract and its notice period are owned and enforced by the HOME, not the family. The LGO decision and the Sandwell/CASCAIDR case both show notice periods are contractual terms the provider controls and enforces (30-day notice demanded; provider liable for breaching its own notice obligations), and the consumer-law guidance frames the home as the contracting counterparty. A solo broker cannot 'transfer' or 'assume' a contract that two families do not control; only the home can consent to early release, and the candidate's OWN commodity_premortem concedes the home 'has no incentive to voluntarily reduce notice-period revenue' and would act adversarially to the broker. So the saving the broker claims to split does not structurally exist unless the home agrees, and the evidence says the home is both the gatekeeper and the disincentivised party. DISTRIBUTION is also unverifiable (0.61): no passage shows any low-friction channel to the broker's actual target (an exiting family mid-notice, or the hospital-social-worker discharge signal); incumbents reach the opposite party (incoming searchers). The lone 'supported' gates are weak and off-thesis: payer_solvency only proves families pay for FINDING-a-home reports, not for notice-period recovery; incumbency merely notes no rival does this exact wedge, which here reads as 'no one validated the market' rather than open field. Net: the central mechanism (notice period as a family-tradable asset) is unproven in pain, unproven in legality, and contradicted by the structural fact that the home controls the contract and is disincentivised to permit transfer.

entries.title: The Kitchen Ninja's Wholesale Price Engine
entries.oneLiner: A vertical SaaS for micro food producers that calculates live cost-per-unit, generates wholesale quotes with nutrition labels, and price-optimises against real-time ingredient markets, preventing profit loss on every sale.
entries.reason: The passage shows Business Butler is an existing food-manufacturing platform that already tracks ingredients, recipes, overhead and profit, handles 'how do I adjust my prices' when ingredient costs rise, includes labor costing, and generates FDA-compliant nutrition, directly covering the candidate's cost-per-unit, pricing and nutrition-label value, so an incumbent already serves this need.

entries.title: NurseSole Mobile, On-Site Shoe Repair & Custom Insoles for Healthcare Workers
entries.oneLiner: A solo operator in a van provides rapid resoling and AI-molded custom insoles to nurses in hospital parking lots, compressing a 2-week podiatrist trip into a 20-minute break.
entries.reason: Passage shows Cobbler.ca already runs a specialized 'Medical & Healthcare' line resoling and reconditioning nurses', surgeons', and paramedics' footwear, so a dedicated incumbent already serves the healthcare-worker footwear-repair need rather than the space being open.

entries.title: The Creative Lead Wire
entries.oneLiner: A paid daily newsletter and SMS alert service that curates overlooked, high-budget brand design RFP opportunities from obscure corporate procurement portals, enriched with insider pitch intelligence sourced from a closed subscriber community.
entries.reason: GovSentry is a funded rival already doing the candidate's core mechanic well: AI-powered round-the-clock monitoring of 100+ procurement portals with smart contract-matched alerts. The space is therefore not greenfield, though GovSentry is government-contract focused (NAICS-matched) rather than the creative/design vertical with win-rate intelligence the candidate claims.

entries.title: The Auto Recall & Hidden Warranty Shakedown
entries.oneLiner: A solo-operated service that uses AI to scan a gig driver's VIN across thousands of TSBs and hidden warranty programs, then aggressively schedules and pressures dealerships to perform repairs at zero cost.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: Not a single one of the six checks reached 'supported', every gate returned 'unverifiable', so under verdict-from-retrieval-only and source-or-die this candidate cannot PASS and must be killed. The decisive failures: (1) The wedge is claimed to be 'proprietary_data' / adversarial detective work, but the retrieved evidence directly undermines that moat. ProblemsByVin already surfaces 'Every recall NHTSA has on file. Every owner complaint they've logged... with the mileage they tend to hit and what the fix costs' across 5,407 vehicles and 78,349 complaints, refreshed weekly, and explicitly 'Free. No signup. No paywall.' The Bumper TSB explainer states a TSB 'is publicly accessible to anyone who knows where to look.' The core data the service would charge to assemble is already a free, public commodity, there is no defensible proprietary-data wedge in the cited record. (2) payer_solvency is unverifiable with ZERO citations, no retrieved passage shows Gen Z gig drivers (explicitly described as having 'no savings buffer') have the budget or willingness to pay for this. A no-savings audience is the worst possible payer for a discretionary, results-uncertain service. (3) pain_reality is unverifiable (0.46): the only evidence describes a latent 'owner advantage', not an active market of people already paying to solve this, no demand signal. (4) distribution is unverifiable (0.43): no channel to reach atomized gig drivers cost-effectively. (5) legality returned 0.0 on an irrelevant bike-taxi-licensing passage, the adversarial 'pressure the dealer' negotiation model is entirely ungrounded as to lawfulness. The idea rests on a proprietary-data claim the evidence refutes (free commodity sources), targets a payer the evidence cannot show can pay, for a pain the evidence cannot show is acute. No grounded basis to publish.

entries.title: The Home-Office Data Shredder
entries.oneLiner: A solo-operated mobile shredding service that provides on-site, certified destruction of sensitive documents for public sector workers, delivering a timestamped, blockchain-anchored digital certificate of GDPR-compliant disposal to protect against personal liability.
entries.reason: The passage shows Iron Mountain, a dominant funded incumbent, already offers on-site certified secure shredding explicitly to reduce liability and ensure compliant destruction, the core need this candidate targets. The space is therefore not underserved by a major established provider.

entries.title: The TinkerTub, Bespoke Hands-On Learning Kits for Primary Teachers
entries.oneLiner: A solo operator designs, assembles, and delivers physical activity tubs mapped to a local primary curriculum, giving time-pressed teachers a grab-and-go hands-on lesson for a fixed per-tub price.
entries.reason: The passage shows TTS, a national educational supplier, already selling a physical 'Move & Learn' activity tub for primary classrooms (£219.99), demonstrating an established incumbent occupies the activity-tub product space the candidate targets. This negates the positive claim that the space is underserved with no dominant incumbent; the passage does not, however, address the candidate's specific hyper-local curriculum-mapping niche.

entries.title: Marine Survey Report Accelerator
entries.oneLiner: A mobile-first vertical tool that helps solo marine surveyors structure inspections, uses AI to auto-detect defects from photos, and auto-populates insurance-ready reports from a curated damage-cost database, cutting report time by 70%.
entries.reason: The passage shows Navalmartin Ltd's 'mir' app, a funded rival already digitising marine surveying for yachts and small crafts, demonstrating the space is not underserved. While its focus is remote/visual surveys rather than report auto-population specifically, it is a funded competitor actively building in the same marine-surveying-digitisation need.

entries.title: The Gig Misclassification Claim Pack
entries.oneLiner: A solo-operated AI tool that automates the building of a tribunal-ready misclassification claim for UK gig workers, combining platform data extraction with precise wage calculations to recover back-dated pay.
