entries.reason: The passage shows CourtCase, a free-to-start tool that ingests emails, contracts, and chat logs, maps them to employment law, surfaces every claim, and produces a judge-ready packet, the candidate's exact value proposition (AI-built, evidence-backed employment claim pack) already offered as a free first-party tool, collapsing the margin for a £149 paid version.

entries.title: The Heritage Tile Matchmaker
entries.oneLiner: A mobile spectrophotometer service that color-matches discontinued ceramic tiles on-site and mixes custom glaze/pigment repair compounds, specialising in Victorian encaustic tiles, saving restoration contractors from full-floor replacements.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The entire thesis rests on one claim: a proprietary, defensible capability 'no paint store or DIY product replicates.' The gathered evidence refutes that moat from three independent directions. (1) Prior art / existing identical service: a tile-restoration business already offers exactly this productized service: 'Quantification and digitization of glaze colors and gloss... Stabilization of quality using spectrophotometers, color difference meters, gloss meters, and color matching by artisans,' reproducing discontinued tiles 'from just one piece'. The on-site spectrophotometer + artisan glaze-match combination is therefore not novel and not proprietary. (2) Granted patent prior art covering scan-and-replicate of discontinued/unavailable tiles (scan original -> 3D model -> CNC -> glaze -> fire) blocks the 'proprietary technical IP' wedge and creates freedom-to-operate risk. (3) The core hardware is a commodity: an off-the-shelf portable colorimeter already matches a substrate shade against 40,000+ references in <2 seconds, and incumbents like Daltile ColorMatch already manufacture color-matched tile to a sample. The differentiation collapses to manual craft (mixing/application), which the candidate itself concedes is the only non-automatable, non-defensible part. Separately, source-or-die fails comprehensively: NOT ONE of the six checks returned 'supported.' There is zero retrieved evidence that the specific pain (UK contractors losing jobs over unmatched Victorian encaustic tiles) is acute and paid, that the SME payers are solvent or willing to pay a premium, or that any low-friction distribution channel to reach them exists. The why-now figure ('listed-building consent surged 23% in 2023') is wholly unverified. An idea whose sole differentiator is shown to be commoditized + already-served + patent-encumbered, and which cannot ground a single positive gate, is not worth building.

entries.title: The Freelancer's Contract Red-Flag Review
entries.oneLiner: A paid weekly newsletter that sources real freelancer contracts, uses AI to flag dangerous clauses, and provides negotiation playbooks backed by a proprietary dataset of clause frequencies and outcomes, now augmented with dispute-resolution data from freelance platforms.
entries.reason: The passage shows ClauseShield, an existing AI-powered contract-analysis product built specifically for freelancers that already delivers risk scoring, plain-English breakdowns, and negotiation-ready redlines backed by a 40,000+ clause database and 70+ risk patterns. That is a direct incumbent solving this exact need well, so the space is not underserved.

entries.title: TreeWise, The Arborist's Risk Report & Quote Engine
entries.oneLiner: A mobile vertical tool for independent tree surgeons that turns job-site observations into council-compliant risk assessments and quotes in minutes, powered by a proprietary condition database that improves with every report.
entries.reason: Passage shows Pro-cess, an existing software product built for tree surgeons offering photo surveys and risk assessment records, so an incumbent already serves this exact niche and the space is not underserved.

entries.title: Deposit Adjudication Outcome Predictor for Inventory Clerks
entries.oneLiner: A mobile tool that gives freelance inventory clerks an adjudication-win probability for every deposit deduction, backed by a growing database of past deposit-scheme decisions and AI vision models that compare damage to thousands of similar cases.
entries.reason: Passage shows DepositDispute, an AI-powered product already serving the UK deposit-adjudication evidence-pack space (DPS, TDS, mydeposits) with the same fair-wear-and-tear and adjudicator-ready value proposition, so a funded/operating rival already addresses this need.

entries.title: HopAlpha, The Nano-Brewery Hop Contract Optimizer
entries.oneLiner: A mobile-first web app that helps nano-breweries (1-5 barrel) manage forward hop contracts, time spot purchases, and forecast alpha acid degradation to slash raw material waste and lock in lower prices.
entries.reason: The passage shows the craft brewery segment entered structural contraction in 2025 with net closures (399 closures vs 335 openings) and volumes down 4.1%, indicating the payer base is financially distressed and shrinking rather than solvent and willing to spend. It addresses the broader craft segment, not nano-tier budgets specifically, but the only evidence available points to a contracting, insolvency-prone payer.

entries.title: The Mark Scheme Mirror, GCSE English Essay Grader for Parents
entries.oneLiner: A web app that uses a proprietary dataset of examiner-marked AQA GCSE English Language Paper 1 essays to give students calibrated grades, assessment-objective breakdowns, and predicted grade boundaries, sold to parents seeking a tutor-level feedback loop at a fraction of the cost.
entries.reason: The passage shows Top Marks AI already provides AI marking for AQA GCSE English Language, achieving a 0.94 correlation with AQA on 16-mark questions, demonstrating an incumbent already solves this need well.

entries.title: The Pension Credit Refusal Forensics Engine
entries.oneLiner: A solo-generated, data-driven appeal dossier for retirees wrongly denied Pension Credit, built from a proprietary FOI-sourced database of local appeal outcomes and tailored argument templates, focusing on capital-threshold and residency misinterpretation cases.
entries.reason: Passage shows Contend Legal already offers an AI-driven service guiding claimants through challenging Pension Credit decisions (mandatory reconsideration), so an incumbent is already serving the appeal need, the space is not open.

entries.title: The Boundary Dispute Evidence Builder
entries.oneLiner: A web app for residential homeowners in England & Wales that compiles a litigation‑ready boundary‑dispute evidence pack using Ordnance Survey MasterMap data, historic aerial imagery, and an AI‑drafted witness statement, turning a £5k solicitor’s job into a £299 DIY product.
entries.reason: The candidate's product compiles a 'litigation-ready boundary-dispute evidence pack,' which is a type of legal bundle. The passage explicitly states that 'BunTool: Make legal bundles in minutes, for free,' indicating that the core value of creating legal bundles is already commoditized and available for free.

entries.title: Gas Safe Register Compliance Notifier for Student Landlords
entries.oneLiner: A solo-operated micro-SaaS that monitors UK student landlords' gas safety certificate expiry dates and automatically dispatches a certified local engineer for the renewal inspection, taking a commission on each booking.
entries.reason: The passage describes 'ComplianceBot, UK Landlord Compliance Tool' which explicitly states it 'reads the expiry dates automatically and tells you when to act' for gas certs, directly addressing the core problem the candidate aims to solve.

entries.title: The Plumber's Cold-Read Estimator
entries.oneLiner: A mobile-first tool that generates instant, fixed-price quotes for emergency plumbing call-outs by combining a visual diagnostic questionnaire with local parts pricing and labour rate data, sold as a monthly subscription to sole-trader plumbers.
entries.reason: The passage describes a free AI plumbing diagnosis tool that identifies problems and estimates costs, directly commoditizing a core value proposition of the candidate's paid service for plumbers. This free alternative negates the durability of the candidate's value.

entries.title: The Zero-Cost Lease Renewal Trigger
entries.oneLiner: A PLG tool that auto-generates and files a rent review or lease renewal notice for commercial tenants in the UK's rising-rent market, taking a 20% cut of the rent reduction or deferral it secures.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The fundamental premise of 'The Zero-Cost Lease Renewal Trigger' is undermined by a complete lack of evidence for the stated pain point. The `pain_reality` check yielded no verifiable information suggesting that small commercial tenants are sufficiently busy or intimidated by the legal process to warrant this tool. Without a validated, significant pain, the market for this product is unproven and potentially non-existent. Additionally, the `legality` check found no information on the regulatory landscape or licensing requirements for automating statutory legal notices in the UK. This introduces significant, unquantified legal and operational risks that could render the idea unfeasible or prohibitively expensive to implement.

entries.title: CareBudgetBot, Direct Payments Compliance Autopilot
entries.oneLiner: Turn messy receipts into a submission‑ready report in one click, eliminating the fear of clawback and keeping your care funds flowing.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The candidate identifies 'Primary carers receiving direct payments or personal health budgets' as the 'who_pays'. However, the `payer_solvency` check is 'unverifiable', stating there is 'no information about the financial capacity or motivation of primary carers receiving direct payments to pay for a compliance tool'. While the pain of financial reconciliation is acknowledged, there is no evidence that this specific, financially anxious and time-poor demographic, receiving funds for care, has the disposable income or willingness to pay for a dedicated SaaS compliance tool. This fundamental lack of verified payer solvency means the projected growth motion cannot be repeatable or scalable, as the core revenue stream is unproven.

entries.title: Retiree Garden Legacy Service
entries.oneLiner: A solo operator designs, plants, and maintains low-maintenance perennial gardens for retirees, then documents the garden's design and care instructions as a 'living legacy' package for their heirs.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The core hypothesis of the 'Retiree Garden Legacy Service' is built upon the assumption that retirees face a dual pain: the physical burden of garden maintenance and an emotional desire to leave a legacy for their heirs. However, the 'pain_reality' check indicates that this premise is unverifiable. The provided source even describes a seventy-year-old retiree actively engaged in starting and maintaining a garden, explicitly stating it 'does not mention any physical burden of maintenance or an emotional desire to leave a legacy for heirs. It does not address whether these are real or acute problems.' This directly undermines the foundational problem the service aims to solve. Without validated pain points, the unique value proposition is severely weakened, as there's no clear evidence that the target audience genuinely experiences the problems this service intends to alleviate.

entries.title: RetireeRentalBridge
entries.oneLiner: Vertical SaaS for retired landlords managing 3-15 rental properties, automating tax, maintenance, and tenant compliance in one dashboard.
entries.reason: The passage describes 'Tenby,' an AI property management platform for small landlords (1-50 units) that automates compliance and handles various landlord tasks, including built-in state laws and AI automations. This directly addresses the core value proposition of RetireeRentalBridge, indicating that the value is already being served and potentially commoditized by existing solutions.

entries.title: NHS Shift Audit API
entries.oneLiner: An API that automatically compares a public sector worker's actual worked shifts against their employment contract and trust policy, flagging unpaid overtime, missed breaks, and contractual breaches, then generates a pre-formatted grievance letter.
entries.reason: The passage describes Phacet as an existing solution that automates payroll consistency checks by cross-referencing payslips and contracts to detect salary, bonus, and contribution errors. This directly refutes the claim that no incumbent solves the need for automated contract-based pay discrepancy detection.

entries.title: Heritage Harvest Assessment Service
entries.oneLiner: A productized service that evaluates an elderly retiree's garden or land for heritage crop potential, monetizing underutilized assets by connecting to high-end culinary and botanical markets.
entries.reason: The passage states that 'Low Consumer Awareness Makes Market-Based Conservation Challenging,' indicating a lack of acute demand or willingness to pay for heritage crops, which refutes the claim of a real and acute problem that people are paying to solve.

entries.title: The Architect's Fee Extractor
entries.oneLiner: A solo-operated service that recovers unpaid design fees from property developers for small architecture practices by filing statutory adjudication claims under the Housing Grants, Construction and Regeneration Act 1996, taking a 25% cut of recovered sums.
entries.reason: The passage explicitly states that Litchfield Malone McDonald (LMM), a law firm, successfully obtained summary adjudication for an architectural firm in a fee dispute. This demonstrates that an incumbent (LMM) already solves the problem of recovering unpaid architectural fees.

entries.title: The Barrister's Brief: Litigation Outcome Predictions as a Service
entries.oneLiner: A solo operator sells probabilistic win/loss predictions for UK civil litigation cases to solicitors and barristers on a per-case basis, using a proprietary spreadsheet model trained on publicly available court judgments.
entries.reason: The passage describes 'CaseRadar', an AI litigation analytics platform that predicts outcomes, analyzes judge patterns, and serves over 2,100 law firms with 45M+ cases indexed, directly refuting the claim that the space is underserved by incumbents.

entries.title: GreenQuote, The Landscaper's Pricing Co-Pilot
entries.oneLiner: An automated estimation tool for elite residential landscape designers that generates highly accurate project quotes by integrating live nursery stock data, local labor rates, and real-time seasonal adjustments.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The market for 'automated estimation tools' that integrate 'live nursery stock data, local labor rates, and real-time seasonal adjustments' for landscape designers is already mature and well-served by established competitors. SiteRecon and YardVision Pro explicitly offer "AI-powered estimates for materials, labor, and margin," directly addressing GreenQuote's core hypothesis of solving "plant cost volatility and misestimated labor" to prevent "margin erosion." SiteRecon is "Trusted by leading property service contractors across North America" and YardVision Pro positions itself as the "#1 AI Platform for Landscapers" with "instant price quotes" and an easy distribution model. This competitive landscape implies that customer acquisition costs (CAC) for GreenQuote would be prohibitively high, as potential customers are already using or have access to comprehensive, similar solutions. Consequently, achieving unit economics that support a living owner income for a small business in this saturated market appears highly unlikely.

entries.title: MedSync Solo, The Pharmacy Revenue Maximiser
entries.oneLiner: A self-serve audit and automation tool for independent pharmacies that sequences medication refill outreach like a playlist, turning chaotic dispensing into a predictable recurring revenue stream.
entries.gateLabel: It did not survive the adversarial pass
entries.reason: The market for automated medication synchronization and refill outreach for independent pharmacies appears to be significantly served by existing and emerging direct competitors, severely challenging MedSync Solo's path to scalable and repeatable growth. The existence of 'Weave Health', offering 'Autonomous AI Agents for Independent Pharmacy' with 'refill check-ins', directly contradicts the assumption of an underserved market. Furthermore, 'AdhereEasy' is an upcoming, HIPAA-ready platform that provides automated refill reminders, an adherence dashboard, and secure patient messaging, targeting independent pharmacies with simple pricing and an active waitlist. These solutions directly address the core value proposition of MedSync Solo, indicating high competition for customer acquisition. While the pain is real, the presence of multiple, established, and well-positioned players already capturing market demand suggests that MedSync Solo would face significant hurdles in establishing a scalable acquisition channel and compounding growth without a highly differentiated and defensible offering.
